skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion component code into MP4 videos through the inference.sh CLI. The skill documents inputs for TSX code, props, dimensions, frame rate, duration, and codec settings.
skill.summary: Render Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos with configurable output settings.
skill.author: toolshell

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, and visible documentation links. No prompt injection or hidden malicious intent was found in SKILL.md. The meaningful risks are documented remote processing of user code through inference.sh and a broad infsh CLI permission pattern.

remediation.issue: Remote processing of component code and props
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy warning that TSX code, props, media URLs, and render settings are sent to inference.sh. Tell users not to include secrets.
Limit allowed tool patterns to the specific infsh commands needed for rendering if the host supports narrower permissions.

static_findings.snippet: > Requires inference.sh CLI (`infsh`). Get installation instructions: `npx skills add inference-sh/s
| `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |
| `composition_id` | string | No | Composition ID to render |
| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |
Your TSX code can import from `remotion` and `react`:
"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export
Render videos from React/Remotion component code via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

semantic_findings.title: Remote Rendering Sends User Code to inference.sh
semantic_findings.description: The skill sends Remotion TSX code, props, and render settings to the inference.sh rendering service. Users could expose sensitive project data if they include secrets or proprietary code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The quick-start example sends a code field to infsh/remotion-render, and the schema defines code and props inputs. This is documented behavior, so the risk is exposure through intended remote processing rather than hidden exfiltration.

semantic_findings.title: Broad inference.sh CLI Tool Scope
semantic_findings.description: The front matter allows Bash(infsh *), which permits any infsh subcommand if enforced by the host tool policy. A narrower command pattern would reduce accidental account changes and unintended remote operations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration is explicit, but the exact command surface depends on the installed infsh CLI and host enforcement. The risk is therefore real but bounded to one named CLI.

content.user_title: Render Remotion Videos from React Code
content.value_statement: Programmatic video work often needs a reliable way to turn React animation code into finished files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through rendering Remotion components with inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Render a default-exported Remotion component into an MP4 video through the infsh CLI.
Accept render settings for width, height, frame rate, duration, codec, and composition ID.
Pass props into the Remotion component for reusable video templates.
Use documented Remotion and React imports for frame-based animation patterns.
Show CLI and Python SDK examples for synchronous and streaming render workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account before rendering.
Sends component code and input data to an external rendering service.
Requires valid Remotion TSX with a default exported component.
Does not create source media assets unless the user provides or generates them elsewhere.

use_cases.title: Create Product Announcement Videos
use_cases.description: Render short branded animations with titles, subtitles, and timed visual sequences for launch updates.

use_cases.title: Automate Data-Driven Clips
use_cases.description: Generate repeatable metric videos by passing props into a reusable Remotion component.

use_cases.title: Prototype Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Turn React animation ideas into MP4 previews with chosen dimensions, frame rate, and duration.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Title Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Use remotion-render to create a three-second MP4 title card. Use a dark background, centered white title text, and a smooth fade-in.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Social Metric Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a square five-second Remotion video that counts from zero to a supplied metric value. Pass the metric label and value as props.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Product Feature Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a 1080p product feature video with three timed sections. Use Sequence timing, fade transitions, and a final call-to-action frame.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Custom Data Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable Remotion render for a data update video. Accept title, subtitle, chart values, colors, duration, FPS, and output dimensions as inputs.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a three-second fade-in title video at 1920 by 1080.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a Remotion component, runs the inference.sh renderer, and returns an MP4 video link.

output_examples.input: A team provides a metric label, target value, and square social video format.
output_examples.output: The skill renders an animated counter clip with the supplied label and final metric value.

output_examples.input: A developer wants a reusable launch video template with props and custom duration.
output_examples.output: The skill structures a prop-driven Remotion component and renders it with the selected timing and dimensions.

best_practices: Keep Remotion components small, deterministic, and focused on one renderable composition.
Review TSX code and props for secrets before sending them to inference.sh.
Set width, height, FPS, and duration explicitly for repeatable video output.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys, private customer data, or unreleased source code into render props.
Do not expect the skill to debug every Remotion runtime error without component context.
Do not use remote media URLs unless licensing, availability, and privacy are acceptable.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion component code into MP4 video files through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it require a local Remotion setup?
faq.answer: The documented workflow uses the inference.sh CLI, so users need infsh installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can I pass data into the video?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents props, so templates can receive titles, numbers, colors, and other structured inputs.

faq.question: Can I change output dimensions?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented inputs include width, height, FPS, duration, composition ID, and codec options.

faq.question: Is my code processed locally?
faq.answer: No. The workflow sends render inputs to inference.sh, so users should avoid secrets and sensitive data.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
